This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/Physical Mode).
2.

This is an application U/S.483 of BNSS by the petitioner for grant of bail in connection with GR Case No. 205 of 2021 arising out of Kodala PS Case No. 614 of 2021 pending in the file of learned Ad-hoc Addl. District and Sessions Judge(FTSC) under POCSO Act, Berhmapur for commission of offences punishable U/Ss.363/ 376(3)/ 376(2)(n)/506 of IPC r/w Section 3(2)(v) of SC & ST (PA)
Act and Section 6 of the POCSO Act, on the main allegation of kidnapping the victim who belongs to "SC" community and committing rape and aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon her by taking advantage of her caste.

3. Heard, Mr. Sunil Kumar Palai, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. P. Satpathy, learned Addl. Public Prosecutor in the matter and perused the record, but none appears for the victim despite being duly informed as apprised by learned Addl. PP.
4 . Admittedly, the Petitioner is in custody since 26.11.2021, but in the meantime, victim has already been examined, however, the trial is yet to be concluded.
Right to speedy trial is the fundamental right of an accused.

Besides, the Petitioner was admitted to interim bail by a Coordinate Bench of this Court in BLAPL No. 8063 of 2023, but the Petitioner has not misused the liberty so granted to him in the form of interim bail.

In such view of the matter and taking into account the long custody of the Petitioner, this Court without expressing any view on merits admits the Petitioner to bail, but subject to certain conditions.

sentences.text:
Hence, the bail application of the Petitioner stands allowed and the Petitioner is allowed to go on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) only with one solvent surety for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin of the case on such terms and conditions as deem fit and proper by it with following conditions:-
(i) the petitioner shall not contact the victim or any of the witnesses of this case (ii) the petitioner shall not threaten the victim and her parental family members, so also shall not induce/influence or coerce any of the remaining witnesses acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts before the Court and (iii) the petitioner shall not visit to the house or village of the victim till disposal of the case.
6. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.

7. Issue urgent certified copy of the order as per Rules.
(G. Satapathy) Judge Priyajit Location: HIGH COURT OF ORISSA D. Surendra Patra vs State Of Odisha ...
